web.title: Vrat Mein Chalega?: Kitty Party Fasting Food Game Rules and Twists
web.description: Vrat Mein Chalega? is a stand or sit kitty party game about fasting food. Rules, a 12 item call list, the disputed items twist, tips and FAQ for 8 to 20 ladies.
web.intro: Vrat Mein Chalega? is a quick, no-props kitty party game where the host calls out a food and every lady decides in 3 seconds whether it is allowed in a vrat (fast): she stays standing for "Chalega" and sits down on her chair for "Nahi chalega". Anyone who gets it wrong or moves too late is out, and the last lady left in the game wins a packet of makhana. The crazy twist is the "jhagda item": for foods families always argue about, like chai or paneer, there is no right answer, so the smaller side of the room is out. It suits an Ekadashi week, a Navratri kitty or any day the ladies are already talking about fasting, and needs nothing but chairs.
materials: One chair per lady, arranged in a row or a circle
A list of 12 to 15 foods for the host, with her answers marked
A phone timer or the host counting to 3
A packet of makhana (or any small prize) for the winner
steps: Before the game, the host writes her call list with answers. A good mix: Sabudana (chalega), Kuttu ki puri (chalega), Makhana (chalega), Aloo (chalega), Singhare ka atta (chalega), Moongfali (chalega), Samak ke chawal (chalega, a tricky one), Chawal (nahi), Gehun ki roti (nahi), Pyaaz (nahi), Saada namak (nahi) and Maggi (nahi).
She also marks 3 "jhagda items" that families argue about, such as Chai, Paneer and Sendha namak wale chips, and keeps them for later in the game.
Every lady stands in front of her own chair, facing the host.
The host calls one food loudly, for example "Sabudana!", and counts to 3.
By the count of 3, each lady must stay standing if she thinks the food is allowed in a vrat (Chalega), or sit down on her chair if it is not (Nahi chalega).
The host then announces the answer from her list. Anyone on the wrong side, and anyone who moved after the count of 3, is out and becomes a judge.
Everyone still in stands up again and the host calls the next food.
When the host calls a jhagda item, there is no right answer: she counts the standing and the sitting ladies, and the smaller group is out. If it is a tie, everyone stays in.
Keep calling until only one lady is left. She wins the makhana packet.
rules: A wrong answer means you are out.
Moving, or changing your mind, after the count of 3 also means you are out.
On a jhagda item, the smaller group is out, whatever they believe at home.
The host's list is the final word, even if your family does it differently.
The last lady still in the game wins.
variations: Ulta round: the host announces that "Chalega" now means sit and "Nahi chalega" means stand, and watches the room get confused.
Ladies who are out become judges and must shout "Vrat toot gaya!" every time someone gets caught.
In the final between two ladies, the host calls foods back to back with no pause until one of them slips.
tips: Every family keeps a vrat a little differently, so say clearly at the start that the host's list decides, and use the jhagda items for the ones people argue about.
Mix easy and tricky foods: samak ke chawal and singhare ka atta catch many ladies out.
Keep the pace fast; the 3 second count is what makes the game funny.
No food is cooked or wasted, so the game works at any point in the kitty, even right after lunch.
Place the chairs with space between them so nobody bumps a neighbour while sitting down quickly.

faq.q: How many players do you need for Vrat Mein Chalega?
faq.a: It works for 8 to 20 ladies, all playing at once. With fewer ladies, play 2 or 3 short rounds.

faq.q: What do you need to play Vrat Mein Chalega?
faq.a: Only one chair per lady, the host's list of foods with answers, and a small prize such as a makhana packet. No food is needed.

faq.q: Which foods are allowed in a vrat for the game?
faq.a: Common "chalega" foods are sabudana, kuttu, singhare ka atta, samak ke chawal, aloo, makhana and moongfali. Common "nahi chalega" foods are rice, wheat, onion and regular salt. Families differ, so the host's list is final.

faq.q: What is a jhagda item in this game?
faq.a: It is a food families argue about, like chai, paneer or sendha namak chips. There is no right answer, so the smaller group of ladies is out.

faq.q: Is Vrat Mein Chalega a good game for an Ekadashi or Navratri kitty party?
faq.a: Yes. It fits any kitty near a fasting day, takes 10 to 15 minutes, needs no props and nobody has to eat anything, so even ladies who are fasting can play.

lines.text: Shruti, is baar kitty mein koi naya game batao na.
lines.say: श्रुति, इस बार किटी में कोई नया गेम बताओ ना।

lines.text: Ek simple game hai, Vrat Mein Chalega. Main step by step batati hun.
lines.say: एक सिंपल गेम हे, व्रत में चलेगा। में स्टेप बाय स्टेप बताती हूँ।

lines.text: Bas kursiyan chahiye, aur jeetne wali ke liye ek makhane ka packet.
lines.say: बस कुर्सियाँ चाहिए, और जीतने वाली के लिए एक मखाने का पैकेट।

label.text: Sab apni kursi ke aage khade

lines.text: Sab ladies apni kursi ke aage khadi ho jaati hain.
lines.say: सब लेडीज़ अपनी कुर्सी के आगे खड़ी हो जाती हें।

lines.text: Host ek khaane ka naam bolti hai, jaise sabudana.
lines.say: होस्ट एक खाने का नाम बोलती हे, जेसे साबूदाना।

lines.text: Agar vrat mein chalta hai toh khadi raho. Nahi chalta, toh turant baith jao.
lines.say: अगर व्रत में चलता हे तो खड़ी रहो। नहीं चलता, तो तुरंत बेठ जाओ।

lines.text: Chai jaise item pe har ghar ka rule alag hota hai. Toh jis taraf kam ladies hon, woh out.
lines.say: चाय जेसे आइटम पे हर घर का रूल अलग होता हे। तो जिस तरफ़ कम लेडीज़ हों, वो आउट।

lines.text: Jo aakhir tak bachi rahe, makhane ka packet uska.
lines.say: जो आख़िर तक बची रहे, मखाने का पैकेट उसका।

lines.text: Bahut easy hai! Agli Ekadashi ki kitty mein yahi khelenge.
lines.say: बहुत ईज़ी हे! अगली एकादशी की किटी में यही खेलेंगे।
